title: Bound-state-mediated remote charging of a quantum battery
authors: Jian-Jian Cheng, Hai-Bo Qiu, Lin Zhang, Ming-Liang Hu
abstract: Remote charging of a quantum battery (QB) is hindered by radiative leakage of the excitation into the photonic environment that acts as a mediator for energy transfer. We consider a charger-battery model consisting of two two-level systems (TLSs) that are locally coupled to two sites of a one-dimensional coupled cavity array. When their transition frequency lies outside the propagation band, the system forms atom-photon bound states with localized photonic components, and the overlap of these components lifts the degeneracy of the even- and odd-parity bound states, yielding an energy splitting that drives coherent energy transfer from the charger to the QB. In this way, the band gap suppresses resonant emission and the localized bound states mediate remote charging. From the parity-resolved spectrum, we relate the charging time to the energy splitting and the charged ergotropy to the fraction of TLS population on the bound states. Bound states closer to the band edge extend the interaction range of the TLSs but contain a large photonic fraction and are consequently more susceptible to photon loss.
summary: This paper investigates how to remotely charge a quantum battery by utilizing the bound states formed when the system's energy lies outside the photonic band gap. The key mechanism is the lifting of degeneracy between even and odd parity bound states, which drives coherent energy transfer. The results show that this bound-state mediation allows for efficient charging, with performance controlled by the separation distance and dissipation rates.
main_problem: The remote charging of a quantum battery (QB) is hindered by energy leakage into the photonic environment.
main_result: The system achieves coherent remote charging when the TLS frequency lies outside the photonic band, forming localized bound states that mediate energy transfer via an even-odd energy splitting.
method: The analysis uses the single-excitation Hamiltonian, solving for bound states and analyzing time evolution using the Lindblad master equation.
model_or_system: The model consists of two two-level systems (TLSs) acting as a charger and a battery, coupled to two sites of a one-dimensional coupled cavity array.
key_observables: Charging time, stored energy ($E_B(t)$), and charged ergotropy ($W_B(t)$).
important_parameters: Separation distance ($d$), detuning ($\delta$), cavity hopping ($J$), and photon loss rate ($\kappa$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are confined to the single-excitation sector, and the analysis often assumes the thermodynamic limit ($N 	o \infty$).
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the setup. Figure 2 displays the four derived bound state energy branches. Figure 5 shows the maximum ergotropy as a function of cavity lifetime and detuning.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the model and the role of the photonic band gap. It then derives the bound state energies and shows how the even-odd splitting facilitates energy transfer. Finally, it analyzes the charging dynamics and the impact of dissipation.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses energy transfer in open quantum systems using engineered photonic structures, which is a core topic in cavity QED and quantum optics.

The four lines outside it are the upper-band even-parity E+,e and odd-parity E+,o, the lower- band even-parity E−,e and odd-parity E−,o branches. (a) E/J vs δ/J at fixed g/J = 2 and d = 2. (b) E/J vs g/J at fixed δ/J = −2 and d = 2. (c) E/J vs d at fixed δ/J = −2 and g/J = 2.
